meta.title: Greek Alphabet
meta.subtitle: 39 letters, letter pairs and signs · both directions, as two cards each
meta.desc: The Greek alphabet as Modern Greek uses it: 39 notes — the twenty-four letters in order, capital and small, with each one's Greek name; then the thirteen two-letter spellings every primer teaches with the alphabet, because Greek writes several single sounds with two letters (ου is "oo", μπ is "b", ντ is "d"); then the two signs, the accent and the diaeresis. The first deck of the Greek collection. Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Every note gives the romanisation the level decks use, the sound described in English words, and one everyday word that shows it, with a speaker beside the letter and the word. Modern Greek writes the sound "ee" six ways (η, ι, υ, ει, οι, υι) and "o" and "e" two ways each, so each of those notes says where that spelling is used — an ending, a stem, a learned word — which is also what tells them apart on the reverse card. The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them; where English has no equivalent — the throaty γ and χ — the card says what to do instead. Sources: the standard description of Modern Greek; the example words' romanisations are English Wiktionary's, via the kaikki.org extraction (CC BY-SA 4.0).

fields.Name: άλφα
fields.Sound: a · a clear, short "a", between the a of cat and the a of father

fields.Name: βήτα
fields.Sound: v · "v" as in van — never a b

fields.Name: γάμμα
fields.Sound: g · before a, o, ou and a consonant, a soft g made far back in the throat, almost gargled; before an e or ee sound, a "y" as in yes

fields.Name: δέλτα
fields.Sound: d · "th" as in this — never a d

fields.Name: έψιλον
fields.Sound: e · "e" as in bed — epsilon, the commoner of the two ways to write it

fields.Name: ζήτα
fields.Sound: z · "z" as in zoo

fields.Name: ήτα
fields.Sound: i · "ee" as in see — eta, the "ee" of the feminine words and endings (η, της, -η)

fields.Name: θήτα
fields.Sound: th · "th" as in thin

fields.Name: γιώτα
fields.Sound: i · "ee" as in see — iota, the plain letter for it; before another vowel often a quick "y" (παιδιά)

fields.Name: κάπα
fields.Sound: k · "k" as in skin, without a puff of breath; before an e or ee sound, nearer the k of keep

fields.Name: λάμδα
fields.Sound: l · "l" as in lamp

fields.Name: μι
fields.Sound: m · "m" as in man

fields.Name: νι
fields.Sound: n · "n" as in net

fields.Name: ξι
fields.Sound: x · "x" as in box — a k and an s together, also at the start of a word

fields.Name: όμικρον
fields.Sound: o · "o" as in pot, short and round — omicron, the commoner of the two ways to write it

fields.Name: πι
fields.Sound: p · "p" as in spin, without a puff of breath

fields.Name: ρο
fields.Sound: r · a tapped or lightly rolled "r", as in Spanish or Scottish English

fields.Name: σίγμα
fields.Sound: s · "s" as in sit; written ς at the end of a word, σ everywhere else

fields.Name: ταυ
fields.Sound: t · "t" as in stop, without a puff of breath

fields.Name: ύψιλον
fields.Sound: y · "ee" as in see — upsilon, romanised y, the "ee" of many words from Ancient Greek

fields.Name: φι
fields.Sound: f · "f" as in fun

fields.Name: χι
fields.Sound: ch · a breathy rasp like the ch of Scottish loch; before an e or ee sound, softer, like the h of huge

fields.Name: ψι
fields.Sound: ps · "ps" as in lapse — also at the start of a word

fields.Name: ωμέγα
fields.Sound: o · "o" as in pot, the same sound as ο — omega, the "o" of the verb ending -ω and of many endings and stems

fields.Name: ου
fields.Sound: ou · "oo" as in food — always these two letters, the only way Greek writes it

fields.Name: αι
fields.Sound: ai · "e" as in bed, the same sound as ε, written with two letters (romanised ai) — the -αι of verb endings

fields.Name: ει
fields.Sound: ei · "ee" as in see, written with two letters (romanised ei) — the -ει of verb endings

fields.Name: οι
fields.Sound: oi · "ee" as in see, written with two letters (romanised oi) — the plural ending -οι

fields.Name: υι
fields.Sound: yi · "ee" as in see, written with two letters (romanised yi) — rare, in a few learned words

fields.Name: αυ
fields.Sound: av · af · "av" before a vowel or a voiced sound (αύριο), "af" before a voiceless one: θ κ ξ π σ τ φ χ ψ (αυτός)

fields.Name: ευ
fields.Sound: ev · ef · "ev" before a vowel or a voiced sound (Ευρώπη), "ef" before a voiceless one (ευχαριστώ)

fields.Name: μπ
fields.Sound: b · mp · "b" as in bed at the start of a word; "mb" or "b" inside one — the only way Greek writes a b

fields.Name: ντ
fields.Sound: nt · "d" as in dog at the start of a word; "nd" or "d" inside one — the only way Greek writes a d

fields.Name: γκ
fields.Sound: gk · "g" as in go at the start of a word; "ng" (as in finger) or "g" inside one

fields.Name: γγ
fields.Sound: ng · "ng" as in finger — never two g sounds

fields.Name: τσ
fields.Sound: ts · "ts" as in cats

fields.Name: τζ
fields.Sound: tz · "dz" as in adze, or nearly the j of jam

fields.Letter: ά έ ή ί ό ύ ώ
fields.Name: τόνος
fields.Sound: the accent (τόνος): marks the stressed syllable of every word of two or more syllables — and changes the word (πότε "when?", ποτέ "never")

fields.Name: διαλυτικά
fields.Sound: the diaeresis (διαλυτικά): the vowel is said apart from the one before it, not as one sound with it (οϊ is "o-ee", where οι is "ee")
fields.Example: κοροϊδεύωkoroïdévoto tease, to make fun of
